frame_ae7bad275eb1.question: Vulnerability analysis of Multipool
artifact_refs: Operator-only rebalance authorization and approved target enforcement
Uniswap V3 mint, burn, collect, swap, and callback flows
TWAP and spot-price validation, including manipulation and stale-observation risks
Position range selection, tick initialization, fee accounting, and reserve updates
ERC20 transfer assumptions, reentrancy exposure, and invariant preservation across deposits and withdrawals

history.rationale: WHY NOW: Multipool is a critical stateful component controlling pooled assets, liquidity positions, swaps, trusted pools, and operator-managed rebalances; its external protocol interactions and price-dependent accounting create the highest immediate risk among unvisited components. EXIT CRITERIA: complete a static trace of every externally callable path and modifier, verify authorization and callback assumptions, reconcile token/reserve/fee invariants before and after each liquidity or swap operation, and document whether any unauthorized loss, accounting divergence, price manipulation, or stuck-funds path exists.

frame_0c759b0814c0.question: Vulnerability analysis of External users and callers
artifact_refs: Caller-controlled deposit and withdrawal flows
Authorization and beneficiary enforcement for Dispatcher-held LP shares
Share-accounting manipulation through repeated or concurrent user actions
Unexpected ERC20 behavior affecting user-facing transfers
Whether user inputs can bypass withdrawal deviation or snapshot protections

history.rationale: WHY NOW: This is the only explicitly identified unvisited component and it sits at the public trust boundary, where caller-directed withdrawals and Dispatcher-held LP shares can expose authorization, accounting, and fund-recipient issues not covered by the completed Multipool analysis. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every externally callable user path into Dispatcher and related contracts; verify caller authorization, share ownership, recipient selection, accounting updates, slippage/deviation checks, and token-transfer ordering; identify any exploitable unauthorized withdrawal, dilution, theft, or denial-of-service path, or document that these invariants hold.

frame_d96aea2b3a0e.question: Vulnerability analysis of Dispatcher
artifact_refs: Deposit and withdrawal accounting using poolInfo and userInfo
Caller-directed withdrawals and LP share ownership
Reserve-based pricing, snapshot-driven state updates, and deviation checks
Interactions with Multipool and ERC20 token transfers
Access control for pool registration and administrative operations

history.rationale: WHY NOW: Dispatcher is an unanalyzed core contract that holds LP shares and mediates user deposits and withdrawals, making it a high-value state and accounting boundary. Its reserve-based pricing, external Multipool/token interactions, and caller-directed withdrawal paths may introduce authorization, stale-accounting, rounding, or reentrancy issues distinct from the completed Multipool and external-user investigations. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace every Dispatcher state transition and external call; verify pool registration and administrative permissions; reconcile deposit, withdrawal, share, reserve, snapshot, and fee calculations across normal and full-withdraw paths; confirm user funds can only be withdrawn by the rightful beneficiary; and document any concrete vulnerability or conclude that these invariants hold.

frame_c8c733f3b848.question: Vulnerability analysis of MultiStrategy
artifact_refs: onlyOwner strategy updates and authorization boundaries
strategy weight-sum validation and zero-weight or duplicate allocation handling
multipool association changes and stale strategy state
effects of strategy updates on downstream rebalance and liquidity accounting

history.rationale: WHY NOW: MultiStrategy is an uncompleted major contract that controls allocation parameters used by the already-flagged Multipool and interacts with owner-managed strategy state. Its update and association paths may introduce authorization, invariant, or stale-state issues that are not covered by the completed Multipool, Dispatcher, or external-caller investigations. EXIT CRITERIA: Review every externally reachable state-changing path and relevant storage/event flow; verify access control, strategy-weight invariants, multipool binding consistency, update ordering, and downstream assumptions; document any concrete vulnerability or conclude no additional issue is supported by static analysis.

frame_5b3d0cfd5f2b.question: Vulnerability analysis of Factory
artifact_refs: multipool creation and initialization
owner and manager permission boundaries
pool registration and duplicate-address handling
deployment bytecode and constructor parameter propagation
external token and pool validation

history.rationale: WHY NOW: Factory is the remaining major protocol component not listed among completed investigations and it creates the Multipool instances that hold user assets; flaws in initialization, authorization, or registration can compromise every deployed pool. EXIT CRITERIA: Trace all creation and administrative flows, verify caller authorization and uniqueness checks, confirm constructor parameters and trusted dependencies are validated and correctly stored, and record any exploitable issue or conclude no material vulnerability is present.
